title: Shop-grade vehicle, job history, and configuration foundation
scope: Add a durable, versioned Vehicle Record and configuration-history foundation around the existing local-first CarbTune workflow, migrate legacy jobs idempotently, support returning vehicles, and prepare technician/audit attribution without authentication or a backend.
objectives: Persist stable Vehicle Records separately from jobs while keeping chassis and installed-engine identity independent.
Support multiple jobs per vehicle and immutable per-job configuration snapshots.
Preserve CT-0059 validation lifecycle truth, unknown facts, archive history, attribution, and existing workflows.
constraints: No PostgreSQL, fake backend, authentication, broad frontend rewrite, or fabricated identity/evidence.
Preserve localStorage compatibility, duplicate/delete safeguards, and protected CT-0058 Git workflow.

acceptanceTests.expected: Legacy migration is safe and idempotent.
acceptanceTests.evidence: Contract and browser migration tests preserve legacy facts, use stable relationships, and never promote historical validation.

acceptanceTests.expected: One vehicle supports multiple immutable jobs/configurations.
acceptanceTests.evidence: Contract and browser tests prove two jobs on one vehicle, carry-forward, unchanged old job/snapshot, and reload persistence.

acceptanceTests.expected: Identity, archive, audit, unknown, and regression rules hold.
acceptanceTests.evidence: Engine-swap chassis separation, archive-preserved jobs, known/UNKNOWN actors, null unknowns, selector, duplicate, delete, responsive, and CT-0059 lifecycle tests all pass.

implementationNotes: The contract envelope is 2.0.0; existing job and validation schemas stay v1, with new independently versioned vehicle/configuration/actor/audit schemas.
Migration joins only an existing relationship or supplied matching VIN; no-VIN legacy jobs remain separate because physical identity is unknown.
Odometer readings are job observations. Return visits deep-clone known current configuration into a new snapshot; vehicle archive is non-destructive.

CT-0058 anomaly: protected wrapper pull was denied .git/FETCH_HEAD inside the restricted sandbox and required explicit narrow escalation although documentation says it should be covered. A repository-scoped policy correction may be appropriate; machine-wide security was not weakened.
Fresh-clone wrapper commit lacked author identity. The established repository identity was supplied only to the protected wrapper process; no Git configuration or permission scope was broadened.

validation.command: npm run validate; git diff --check; node --check data/service-contracts.js
validation.summary: All 6 canonical programs passed; 35,036 vehicle records, Vehicle/Chassis browser regressions, and 165 workflow/persistence/responsive assertions passed. Static syntax and diff checks passed.
